answer.exemplar: Distinguishing cause from accompaniment requires evidence of mechanism and counterfactual dependence, not just temporal sequence, to avoid confusing correlation with causation.

questions.explanation: Distinguishing cause from accompaniment requires evidence of mechanism and counterfactual dependence, not just sequence, to avoid confusing correlation with causation.
questions.hint: Ask what evidence separates cause from accompaniment.
